## Findings from this iteration

Running the backtest against period 1 surfaced **two blocking problems that
had to be resolved before any period can be meaningfully evaluated**:

### Finding 1 — the theory rule files were unparseable

The very first diagnostic line of the backtest was:

```
[theory] failed to parse technical.yaml: while scanning a simple key
  in "docs/technical.yaml", line 432, column 13
[theory] rules loaded: technical=0 keys, cot=11 keys
```

In other words, every previous invocation of the backtest was running against
an **empty technical.yaml rule set**. The engine was not actually exercising
the Phase 1 refinements at all.

Three separate YAML defects were uncovered in sequence:

1. **`docs/technical.yaml` line 431** — the `COT (Commitment of Traders)`
   bullet under `sentiment.key_elements` spanned two lines, the first with
   a colon that YAML interpreted as starting a mapping. The continuation
   line then failed to parse as a mapping value.
2. **`docs/technical.yaml` line 908** — the `interbank_reality
   .there_is_no_single_algorithm` list item started with a quoted string
   (`"IPDA / ebitda"`) followed by unquoted trailing text on the same line,
   which is not valid YAML.
3. **`docs/terms.yaml` line 598** — the `Curva de aprendizaje` English
   definition contained an unquoted `four stages:` inside a folded scalar,
   which the YAML scanner flagged as `mapping values are not allowed here`.

After the three fixes, all three theory files parse clean:

```
technical OK
cot OK
all OK
```

### Finding 2 — more than a syntax fix: a content contradiction

The first of the three defects was not just a typo. The bullet at
`technical.yaml` line 431-432 read:

> `COT (Commitment of Traders): tracks commercials (makers/institutions)
> vs speculators. Weekly driver for BTC/ETH bias. Commercials move the market.`

That framing **directly contradicts the Phase 1 refinement** in
`cot_integration.yaml` and `contradictions.md §4`, which explicitly corrected
the "COT as weekly driver" error and re-labelled commercials as
*defensive hedgers who provide liquidity, not directional drivers*. The stale
line survived Phase 1 because nothing was reading
`sentiment.key_elements` — the file did not parse.

The fix **replaces the stale framing with a reference-not-driver phrasing
that matches the rewritten `cot_integration.yaml`**, and points the reader
at `weekly_decision_order` for the actual COT precedence contract. This is
the single concrete theory improvement for iter 1: close the gap between
the `sentiment` section in `technical.yaml` and the refined
`cot_integration.yaml`.

### Finding 3 — 4H/1H data gap for this period (logged, not yet resolved)

Even with rules loading, the period 1 backtest cannot progress past data
loading. The only local 4H file is
`data/hyperliquid_snapshots/BTC_4h.parquet`, which starts **2023-12-26**;
the OpenBB fallback refuses `interval=4h` because the underlying provider
(yfinance) only accepts `1h`, `1d`, etc. The same gap exists for ETH.

Per AGENTS.md the correct action for a data gap is *log and continue*. The
gap is logged here and, by extension, will apply to iter 2 through iter 5
(all periods before 2023-12-26). The effective earliest period that can
exercise the full weekly → 1H pipeline is **2024-ETF-approval** (period 7).

## What changed and why

**One concrete theory improvement** (plus the two incidental syntactic
fixes that the first improvement required in order to land):

- `docs/technical.yaml` `sentiment.key_elements` — the COT bullet now
  matches the Phase 1 refinement. It explicitly states that COT is a
  weekly **reference**, not driver; that commercials are defensive hedgers
  who provide liquidity rather than drive direction; and it cross-refers
  to `cot_integration.yaml` for the full usage contract.

Why: without this fix, the `sentiment` section was silently telling any
future consumer of the YAML the opposite of what `cot_integration.yaml`
says. And because the file did not parse, the backtest engine was running
with `technical=0 keys` — every previous theoretical claim in the Phase 1
changelog was being ignored by the engine.

Incidental fixes bundled in the same commit because they were prerequisites
to making the first fix observable:

- `docs/technical.yaml` line 908 — quoted-then-unquoted scalar fixed.
- `docs/terms.yaml` line 598 — folded-scalar with embedded colon quoted.

No new sections added, no existing semantics deleted.

## 4H/1H execution notes

Not applicable for this iteration — no data was available to evaluate

later iterations: if 4H data cannot be obtained for any pre-2023 period,
the theory's 4H/1H execution contract will only be tested on periods 7, 8,
